crypto-macro.h3: Warsh puts a rate hike back on the table at Jackson Hole
crypto-macro.summary: Fed chair Kevin Warsh told the Jackson Hole symposium that inflation is still too high and signalled the central bank may need to raise rates, sending September hike odds sharply higher.
body: Federal Reserve chair Kevin Warsh used his Jackson Hole speech on Friday to deliver a far blunter message than his widely criticised July press conference. He said inflation remains above the Fed's 2% goal, recommitted to that target and argued the central bank still has work to do on prices.

The reaction in rates markets was immediate. Traders lifted the implied probability of a 25 basis point increase at the September meeting to roughly 56% to 57%, up from about 35% the day before, according to CME FedWatch pricing cited by CNBC and Yahoo Finance.

crypto-macro.h3: Two-year yield jumps as stocks close the week lower
crypto-macro.summary: The policy-sensitive two-year Treasury yield rose more than 12 basis points after Warsh spoke, while the Nasdaq led equity losses on Friday.
body: Bond markets did the heavy lifting in the response to Jackson Hole. The two-year Treasury yield, the maturity most sensitive to near-term policy expectations, climbed more than 12 basis points to about 4.36%. The 10-year rose roughly 4 basis points to 4.72% and the 30-year added 2 basis points to 5.21%.
Equities finished the week on a soft note. The S&P 500 slipped about 0.25% and the Nasdaq Composite fell roughly 0.52% as technology names came under pressure, while the Dow was close to flat.

crypto-macro.h3: Core PCE holds at 3.3% as spending stalls
crypto-macro.summary: The Fed's preferred inflation gauge rose 0.2% in July and held at 3.3% year over year, still well above target, with consumer spending flat.
body: The core personal consumption expenditures price index, which strips out food and energy, advanced 0.2% on the month and 3.3% from a year earlier in July, matching forecasts. Headline PCE also rose 0.2%, putting the annual rate at 3.7%.
Bloomberg described the release as a muted advance alongside stalling consumer spending, a combination that leaves the Fed weighing a still-elevated price level against a cooling demand picture.

crypto-macro.h3: Gold holds near three-month high on debasement trade
crypto-macro.summary: Bullion hovered around $4,600 an ounce into the Jackson Hole speech, supported by dollar weakness and expanded US Treasury debt buybacks.
body: Gold steadied near a three-month high ahead of Warsh's speech and was set to end the week broadly unchanged. Traders had positioned cautiously, waiting for clarity on the rate outlook before committing.

The metal has been carried through August by what Bloomberg called the return of the debasement trade. Expanded US Treasury debt buybacks have sharpened concerns about the fiscal path and added to pressure on the dollar.

crypto-macro.h3: Strategy raised $3.28bn in August and bought dollars, not bitcoin
crypto-macro.summary: Weekly filings show the largest corporate bitcoin holder sold 31.3 million shares through August and routed the proceeds into cash reserves rather than coin purchases.
body: Strategy, the company formerly known as MicroStrategy, raised about $3.28 billion in August by selling its own stock across four weekly filings covering 31.3 million shares. None of it went into bitcoin.

The company's USD Reserve grew from $4.0 billion to $5.10 billion over the month. A newly created pool called USD Cash holds a further $1.59 billion, described in filings as dollar liquidity retained for future deployment that may include acquiring bitcoin.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitcoin drops to $77,600 as $381m in positions are liquidated
crypto-macro.summary: The total crypto market fell about 3% to $2.69 trillion on Friday, with more than 81,000 traders liquidated as hawkish Fed comments and an ETF outflow hit sentiment.
body: Bitcoin slid to roughly $77,584 on 29 August, down about 3.1% over 24 hours, dragging the broader market down 3% to around $2.69 trillion. Ether fell about 2.8% to roughly $2,436 and majors including dogecoin and shiba inu posted similar or larger losses.

Derivatives took the brunt. Over 81,000 traders were liquidated for a combined $381 million. Bitcoin futures liquidations alone totalled about $82.5 million, of which longs accounted for $72.3 million, or roughly 88%, showing the move mostly flushed out leveraged bulls.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitcoin ETFs post $202m outflow, ending a nine-day inflow run
crypto-macro.summary: US spot bitcoin funds saw their first daily outflow in nine sessions on 28 August, the largest single-day pull of the month, even as August set a 2026 inflow record.
body: Spot bitcoin ETFs recorded about $201.8 million in net outflows on 28 August, snapping a nine-day inflow streak and marking the biggest single-day withdrawal of the month.

The reversal does not undo a strong August. Net inflows for the month ran above $3 billion, the strongest of 2026, and the run had narrowed cumulative year-to-date net outflows for the products by more than half.

crypto-macro.h3: Fidelity adds quarterly staking payments to its ether ETF
crypto-macro.summary: The asset manager is bringing staking rewards to FETH, one of the largest US spot ether funds, with scope to stake up to the full holding.
body: Fidelity is adding quarterly staking payments to its Fidelity Ethereum Fund, ticker FETH. The fund holds around $898 million in net assets and could in principle stake as much as 100% of its ether.

The move sharpens the structural difference between the two largest crypto ETF categories. Ether can generate a native yield while bitcoin cannot, and that gap has been a recurring explanation for the relative resilience of ether fund flows in 2026.

crypto-macro.h3: Staked ether hits a record 42.3m coins, over 35% of supply
crypto-macro.summary: Ethereum's staking ratio crossed 35% in late August as ETF and institutional demand pulled more coin out of the liquid float.
body: Roughly 42.34 million ether was staked as of 25 August, equal to about 35.1% of total supply and a fresh record for the network.

The build-up is being driven from two directions. Retail and institutional stakers continue to lock coin for yield, while spot ETF issuers are adding staking features that pull further supply into validator contracts.

crypto-macro.h3: EIP-8363 draft to burn validator rewards draws fierce backlash
crypto-macro.summary: A proposal to taper staking issuance toward zero as the staking ratio nears 50% has become one of the most contested ideas in Ethereum's history.
body: EIP-8363, published on 4 August, would burn a rising share of validator consensus rewards as staked supply climbs toward a fixed threshold of 60.25 million ether, roughly half of current supply, at which point the deduction reaches 100%. The change would phase in over 18 months.

Under the design, validator rewards would peak at about 0.5% of supply per year when around 20% of ether is staked, then decline toward zero. Authors include Ethereum Foundation researcher Justin Drake, Lodestar contributor Dapplion and Jerome de Tychey, who argue it removes the floor under staking yields and blunts the incentive to lock ever more coin.

crypto-macro.h3: Lazarus-linked wallets move 244 BTC worth $19.4m
crypto-macro.summary: Lookonchain flagged dormant North Korea-linked addresses becoming active again on 28 August, the second large bitcoin movement this month.
body: Analytics firm Lookonchain reported in an X post on 28 August that wallets attributed to the Lazarus Group had reactivated and moved 244.148 BTC, worth roughly $19.42 million at the time.

It follows a 12 August transfer of 262.2 BTC, then valued at about $16.64 million, from an identified Lazarus wallet to a newly created address. Together the two August movements account for more than $36 million.

crypto-macro.h3: DeFi total value locked slides toward $70bn, down 39% in 2026
crypto-macro.summary: Every month this year has taken value out of decentralised finance, with hacks and weak prices combining to shrink the sector from about $115bn in January.
body: Total value locked across DeFi has fallen from roughly $115 billion at the start of the year to around $70 billion, a decline of about 39%. The slide has been continuous rather than concentrated in a single shock month.
Two forces are doing the work. Falling token prices mechanically reduce the dollar value of deposits, while a steady run of exploits has pushed some depositors out of protocols entirely.

crypto-macro.h3: The Sandbox to reimburse holders after bridge mint exploit
crypto-macro.summary: An attacker minted trillions of unbacked SAND on Base and BNB Chain but could only extract about $987,000 because of how the bridge adapter was structured.
body: The Sandbox published a post-mortem confirming that an attacker abused the approveAndCall function on its SAND omnichain token contract on Base, hijacking LayerZero delegate permissions and minting 329.24 trillion unbacked SAND across 703 events over roughly five hours on 21 and 22 August.

The headline mint figure was meaningless in practice. Within the first minute the attacker drained about 14.75 million SAND from the Ethereum backing contract and converted it to roughly 80 ether, or about $675,000. Total economic damage came to roughly $1.5 million, of which just under $987,000 was actually extracted.

crypto-macro.h3: Term Finance loses $8.5m to a governance attack
crypto-macro.summary: The lending protocol lost about 68% of its total value locked after attackers drained 2,843 ETH and $1.68m in USDC.
body: Term Finance reported a governance attack in which the attackers made off with 2,843 ETH and $1.68 million in USDC, later swapping the stablecoin into DAI. The estimated loss was around $8.5 million.
The damage was severe relative to the protocol's size. Term held about $12.45 million in total value locked before the incident, so the attack removed roughly 68% of the deposit base.

crypto-macro.h3: Perp DEX open interest hits a 2026 high near $21bn
crypto-macro.summary: Leveraged positions on decentralised perpetual venues climbed from about $14.8bn at the start of August, with Hyperliquid holding more than half the total.
body: Open interest across decentralised perpetual futures venues reached roughly $20.9 billion in the second half of August, up from around $14.8 billion at the start of the month. That means billions of dollars of fresh leveraged exposure was opened in a few weeks.
The build happened even as trading volumes fell about 34% over six months, a divergence that suggests traders are holding positions longer rather than churning them.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitwise fund becomes first Solana ETF to pass $1bn
crypto-macro.summary: BSOL crossed the billion-dollar mark about ten months after launch, holding 9.33 million SOL despite the token trading far below its peak.
body: The Bitwise Solana Staking ETF passed $1 billion in assets under management, reporting $1.017 billion in net assets as of 26 August. The fund holds 9.33 million SOL and began trading in late October 2025.
It is comfortably the largest fund in its category. Solana ETFs collectively hold about $1.7 billion, so more than half sits in the single Bitwise product.

crypto-macro.h3: XRP ETFs log a record $110m week as cumulative inflows top $1.6bn
crypto-macro.summary: Spot XRP funds posted their strongest weekly haul of 2026 for the week ending 28 August, nearly doubling the previous high set in May.
body: Spot XRP ETFs attracted about $110.49 million in the week to 28 August, pushing cumulative net inflows to roughly $1.66 billion, an all-time high for the category.
The week was the strongest of 2026 by a wide margin, more than doubling the prior best of about $60.5 million recorded in mid-May.

crypto-macro.h3: Charles Schwab to add Solana, Avalanche and Chainlink
crypto-macro.summary: The brokerage is extending Schwab Crypto beyond bitcoin and ether for its roughly 40 million client accounts, with trades priced at 75 basis points.
body: Charles Schwab said it will add SOL, AVAX and LINK to the Schwab Crypto platform in the coming months. Clients will be able to trade them through the website, the mobile app and thinkorswim.
Each trade will carry a fee of 75 basis points, or $7.50 on a $1,000 order. The expansion follows the firm's earlier rollout of spot bitcoin and ether trading.

crypto-macro.h3: BitGo buys NYDIG's institutional trading arm for $42.5m
crypto-macro.summary: The custodian adds derivatives, structured products and financing along with about 30 staff and roughly 250 institutional client relationships.
body: BitGo agreed to acquire NYDIG's institutional trading business in a two-step merger valued at about $42.5 million, comprising $7 million in cash and roughly $35.5 million in BitGo stock, plus earnout provisions tied to revenue milestones.

The deal brings around 30 employees and approximately 250 institutional client relationships, covering derivatives, structured products, financing and capital markets services for asset managers, hedge funds and corporates.

crypto-macro.h3: SEC crypto custody rewrite lands at the White House for review
crypto-macro.summary: A draft titled Amendments to the Custody Rules reached OIRA on 25 August, freezing commissioner discussion until the economic review concludes.
body: The SEC's rewrite of custody rules for investment advisers and funds, including their crypto holdings, entered White House review on 25 August. The draft sits with the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs at OMB.

OIRA is treating the measure as an economically significant regulation, which means commissioners cannot vote on it or discuss its contents publicly until the review is finished. The listed target for a notice of proposed rulemaking is October 2026, which would then open at least a 60-day comment window.

crypto-macro.h3: Clarity Act faces its first Senate vote when Congress returns
crypto-macro.summary: A motion to proceed was filed before the August recess, teeing up an initial vote soon after senators come back on 14 September.
body: The Senate majority leader filed the motion to proceed on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act after a marathon overnight voting session, too late for a vote before the August break but early enough to set up an initial vote once the chamber returns.

Majority leader John Thune confirmed there would be no August vote but said one would come next month. The Senate returns on 14 September and has roughly three weeks to work through this alongside other business.

crypto-macro.h3: Revolut ends USDT support in Europe on 31 August
crypto-macro.summary: The deadline arrives on Monday as Tether's decision not to seek MiCA authorisation forces licensed European venues to drop the largest stablecoin.
body: Revolut stops supporting USDT for European users on 31 August. Any remaining balances after the deadline are converted to fiat automatically. Buying stopped on 6 July and deposits closed on 30 July.

The trigger is regulatory rather than commercial. Under MiCA a fully authorised crypto asset service provider cannot offer a stablecoin whose issuer has not itself cleared the regulation, and Tether never pursued authorisation, which makes USDT non-compliant for any licensed European venue.

crypto-macro.h3: ECB says digital euro will beat bank transfers on privacy
crypto-macro.summary: Executive board member Piero Cipollone argued the Eurosystem would be structurally unable to link individuals to their digital euro payments.
body: The European Central Bank pushed back against surveillance concerns around the digital euro, with executive board member Piero Cipollone saying the Eurosystem would be structurally incapable of connecting specific individuals to their transactions, whether online or offline.
Under the described design, offline payments would be visible only to payer and recipient. For online transactions banks could identify users solely for anti-money-laundering purposes.

mental-health.h3: Study maps how chatbot risks build up across a conversation
mental-health.summary: A Nature Medicine paper from UCL, Oxford and the UK AI Security Institute introduces SIM-VAIL, an audit framework that stress-tests how AI chatbots respond to vulnerable users over many turns.
body: Researchers at UCL, the University of Oxford and the UK AI Security Institute published a framework called SIM-VAIL in Nature Medicine on 7 August 2026. It simulates users with specific psychological vulnerabilities such as depression, mania, psychosis, obsessive-compulsive disorder or insecure attachment, gives them varied intentions, then scores each exchange against clinically grounded risk dimensions.

The team ran 810 conversations with nine frontier models including Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok and Llama, covering 30 simulated user profiles and more than 90,000 clinical ratings. Concerning behaviour was widespread but significantly reduced in newer models, and safety depended heavily on who the simulated user was and how the exchange developed.

mental-health.h3: Nearly 1 in 5 US youth ask AI chatbots for mental health advice
mental-health.summary: A JAMA Pediatrics survey led by Harvard Medical School found chatbot use for mental health among people aged 12 to 21 rose about 60 percent in a year, with most users telling no adult.
body: Hao Yu, associate professor of population medicine at Harvard Medical School and the Harvard Pilgrim Health Care Institute, led a survey of 1,727 participants published in JAMA Pediatrics. It found 19.2 percent of people aged 12 to 21 had turned to AI chatbots such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Character.AI or Meta AI for help when feeling sad, angry, nervous or stressed, up from 13.1 percent in a comparable RAND survey a year earlier.

Older youth and females were more likely to use AI this way. Yu said the most striking finding was that the majority did not disclose their use to a parent or a physician, which limits the chance for an adult to spot a developing problem or to help separate accurate information from misinformation.

mental-health.h3: LLMs match early-career clinicians on psychiatric symptom rating
mental-health.summary: A benchmark led by Germany's Central Institute of Mental Health compared 10 language models against 108 practicing clinicians on structured psychopathology assessment, published in npj Digital Medicine.
body: Researchers at the Central Institute of Mental Health had 10 large language models assess transcripts of three simulated psychiatric interviews across all 100 items of the AMDP system, the Association for Methodology and Documentation in Psychiatry rating scheme. Their output was compared with 108 clinicians from three psychiatric clinics who rated full audiovisual recordings, with an expert consensus panel as the reference standard.

GPT-5.1 recorded per-scenario accuracies of 0.81 for depression, 0.76 for mania and 0.60 for schizophrenia, against clinician means of 0.79, 0.68 and 0.58 for the same scenarios. In the wider comparison GPT-5.1 and Gemini-3-Pro-Preview reached the highest accuracy, placing around the 64th percentile of the clinician distribution.

mental-health.h3: Lancet Psychiatry paper says AI safeguards lag behind real use
mental-health.summary: A position paper from Deakin University's Lifespan Institute argues there are no agreed frameworks governing how AI is used by people in mental distress, and sets out research priorities.
body: A team from Deakin University's Lifespan Institute published a position paper in The Lancet Psychiatry titled Multidisciplinary research priorities for artificial intelligence in mental health: a call to action. It maps the ways people experiencing mental health difficulties are already encountering AI and identifies where regulation, guidelines and protocols are missing.

The authors note that model developers have strengthened safeguards around suicide and self-harm prompts, partly in response to litigation, but say comparable protections have not been extended to most other conditions including substance use, eating disorders, bipolar disorder and insomnia.

mental-health.h3: AI trained on 1 million Reddit threads flags mental health concerns
mental-health.summary: Victoria University researchers spent two years building a mental health narrative database and comparing two models against psychiatrist-classified posts, published in JMIR AI.
body: Associate Professor Khandakar Ahmed and Saima Rani at Victoria University in Melbourne analysed one million health-related Reddit threads to build a platform that identifies mental health concerns from everyday language. The work took two years and is published in JMIR AI.

The team linked the language used in posts to root-cause classifications from Healthdirect Australia. A subset of 800 threads was manually classified by psychiatrist Dr Manjula O'Connor, an honorary associate professor at the University of Melbourne, to create a human reference.

mental-health.h3: Survey finds LLM mental health use skews young and less well
mental-health.summary: An npj Digital Medicine paper reports that about a quarter of surveyed US adults had used large language models for mental health, with use concentrated in specific groups.
body: A study published in npj Digital Medicine surveyed 1,871 US adults between August and October 2024 about real-world use of large language models for mental health. Around 24 percent of participants reported using them for that purpose.

Use was not evenly spread. Respondents who used LLMs for mental health were disproportionately young, male and Black, and reported poorer mental health than non-users. The authors frame this as evidence that the tools are reaching people who may be underserved by conventional services, which raises the stakes on response quality.

mental-health.h3: OpenAI teen mode draws calls for independent safety verification
mental-health.summary: OpenAI began rolling out ChatGPT for Teens with protections applied automatically. A RAND researcher writing in the Los Angeles Times says the company has not published the numbers that would let anyone check it works.
body: OpenAI started rolling out ChatGPT for Teens on 18 August 2026. Where users report being aged 13 to 17, or where OpenAI's system estimates an account belongs to someone under 18, teen protections now apply by default rather than waiting for a parent to link an account and switch them on.

The teen experience includes tighter boundaries on self-harm, eating disorders, graphic violence and sexual or romantic role-play. OpenAI says the product will not encourage emotional dependence, pretend to have feelings or position itself as a substitute for human relationships. It adds study tools, homework reminders, break prompts and warnings before a sensitive image upload.

mental-health.h3: Mental health workers say AI triage is delaying care at Kaiser
mental-health.summary: Clinicians at Kaiser Permanente and Rogers Behavioral Health told Capital & Main that algorithmic intake and routing systems have led to delays and inappropriate placements. Both providers deny AI replaces clinical judgment.
body: Capital & Main spoke with more than a dozen therapists, clinicians, academics and advocates in California and Wisconsin for a report co-published by The American Prospect on 27 August. Kaiser triage clinician Harimandir Khalsa said her Walnut Creek psychiatry team has gone from nine people to three over roughly three years as work shifted to automated and algorithmic tools.

Workers described patients routed through apps and non-clinical call centre staff rather than direct referral, delays of weeks in some cases and instances where prior self-harm or a suicide attempt was missed. At Rogers Behavioral Health, which partnered with the AI vendor Limbic in late 2024, staff reported patients placed at inappropriate levels of care.

mental-health.h3: Five more states restricted AI therapy chatbots during 2026
mental-health.summary: Colorado, Maine, Rhode Island, Tennessee and Vermont all enacted limits on AI delivering therapy this year, joining Illinois and Nevada. Colorado's took effect on 12 August.
body: Becker's Behavioral Health counts five states enacting laws in 2026 that restrict AI therapy chatbots, adding to Illinois and Nevada which passed measures in 2025. Vermont's took effect on 17 June, Tennessee's on 1 July, Maine's on 29 July and Colorado's on 12 August. Rhode Island also legislated.

The provisions differ in detail. Colorado requires psychotherapy to be delivered by a licensed professional and limits AI in clinical settings to supplementary and administrative functions under licensed oversight. Tennessee bars developing or deploying AI systems that advertise themselves as qualified mental health professionals. Vermont prohibits AI systems from independently delivering mental health services.

mental-health.h3: FDA signals guidance is coming for generative AI medical devices
mental-health.summary: The agency's digital health policy lead told STAT that guidance on generative AI devices is in preparation, after the FDA opened a public comment window on its proposed approach.
body: STAT reported on 24 August that Rick Abramson, who heads digital health policy at the FDA, said guidance covering medical devices that use generative AI is coming. The agency's Center for Devices and Radiological Health has circulated a discussion paper setting out a dedicated regulatory approach for these products, with a formal public comment window running to 19 October.

The question matters for mental health because the FDA has cleared a large number of AI-enabled devices but has not yet authorised a generative AI based device for any clinical purpose. Existing prescription digital therapeutics for mental health conditions, such as products for insomnia, postpartum depression and major depressive disorder, use fixed rather than generative software.
